verdicts.note: Refers to herself among 'the girls' (vs 'the boys'); 'two of us are girls' elsewhere — clearly female.
Currently on her 'year out'/placement, returning to final year in October — placement year.
Entire interview is about her current placement; started 'middle of July last year' — yes.
Same quote as 'industry'; supports work-experience value but is really about seeing industry — agree adequate, confidence trimmed.
'to see like an industry that actually involves engineering... Its good to see it' maps directly to seeing what industry is like.
Calls personal growth 'the best thing'; repeatedly stresses learning about herself/handling people — strongly agree well-supported.
Direct 'Yes' that placement helps get a job; aware of skills at interview — agree supported.
Mentions the year 'can contribute... to be Chartered' only as an aside, not framed as a reason she wanted placement — thin; downgrade.
Links placement to the DIS dissertation content, but not to DECIDING a project nor as a reason for placement — inferential; downgrade.
'I needed the year out' after an extra foundation/college year supports needing a break from education — agree.
Explicit 'No... I still can't focus on a particular area' to 'does it help you decide' — disagree clearly supported.
'Production stuff' is about placement role exposure; she repeatedly states 'I still can't focus on a particular area' — don't know is more faithful than manufacturing.
Could take business/managerial or technical route; explicitly can't focus — don't know supported.
'definitely so varied... the word engineering just doesn't justify it'; though prompted, she elaborates emphatically in own words — strongly agree.
'It is interesting - yes definitely very interesting' — direct strongly agree.
Answers a factual question that travel opportunities exist; never says travel is IMPORTANT to a job decision — does not support the importance construct.
Says uni has 'more of a competitive edge'; 'Yes definitely' to uni being more competitive — agree supported.
Quote concedes uni gives 'a lot of teamwork or group work' opportunity ('not the same' as work); weak basis for disagree — downgrade, near-neutral.
Uni group work 'like a chore... oh not group work again' — dissatisfied supported.
'silly to rule it out' is about not ruling out an engineering CAREER, a mild double-negative, not 'pleased I chose to STUDY' — positive disposition but thin; downgrade.
